frozen.ladderDefinition: BU-C0's reception-option ladder VERBATIM (L1 position on Q07's own ±2 m band extracted from src/sim/mechanics.ts:419 · L2 the engine's own flight prediction · L3 `arrivalMargin > 0` · L4 the engine's corridor sampler), with the powerMultiplier threaded into L2/L3/L4 through the ORACLE'S OWN parameter. Commensurable with BU-C0 / BU-T0 / BU-T0b / BU-T1 by construction.

populations.reception: every tick at which the ball's owner CHANGES while phase === "playing".
populations.pressedReception: a reception whose receiver has an opponent within 4.2 m (TOUCH_CONTROL_DIST, src/sim/constants.ts:315).
populations.pressedCarrierMoment: a NON-reception carrier tick sampled every 12 ticks (0.2 sim-s) at which the carrier is pressed.
populations.survivingOption: an L1∧L2∧L3∧L4 option AT THAT RUNG; the receiving-cost and overshoot faces are measured on THIS population only (the set a chooser could actually pick from).

pipeline: 1. CHOICE — `performPass(match, passer, mate, offsideExempt, powerChoice = 1)` (src/sim/mechanics.ts). The weight INPUT already exists.
2. THE ONLY POWER CLAMP — `intended = clamp(powerChoice, 0.85, 1.15)` (src/sim/mechanics.ts:370). Occurrences in src: 1.
3. LEAD — `flight = dist / (16 · orientation·intended)`, receiver led by `vel · flight · 0.8`. The passer leads on what he MEANT.

4. EXECUTION ERROR — `executedPassPower`: gaussian × |intended−1| × 0.6 × (1.35 − passing), clamped to [0.7, 1.3]. At intended === 1 it returns 1 and draws NO RNG — which is why every live call is byte-identical today.
5. STRIKE — `speed = clamp(d·0.6 + 8.2, 9, 22) · executedMul` (src/sim/mechanics.ts:392). ⭐ THE CLAMP IS APPLIED TO THE DISTANCE LAW, THEN MULTIPLIED.
6. THE ORACLE MIRROR — `predictGroundPass` (src/ai/prediction.ts:65): the SAME law, but power is FLOORED ONLY (`max(0.1, powerMultiplier)`, src/ai/prediction.ts:55) and carries NO execution error.
7. FRICTION — `groundBallTravelTime` walks the engine's own geometric series (decay = exp(−0.55·DT) per tick); the range ceiling is launchSpeed × 1.826528 m.

9. PROPAGATION — the multiplier reaches `evaluatePassAffordance` (src/ai/passAffordance.ts:89), `evaluatePassCorridorInterception` (src/ai/passCorridorInterception.ts:84) and `evaluatePassOption` (src/ai/passOptionValue.ts:123) — every one of them defaults it to 1.

honestyVerdict.theOnlyDIVERGENCE: ⭐⭐ the SIM clamps the CHOSEN power to [0.85, 1.15]; the ORACLE only FLOORS it at 0.1. INSIDE the sim clamp the two agree exactly; OUTSIDE it the oracle keeps pricing a ball the sim would never strike.
honestyVerdict.theSecondDIVERGENCE: the oracle prices the INTENDED power; the sim strikes the EXECUTED one (gaussian, σ = |p−1|·0.6·(1.35 − passing)). At p = 1 the error is identically 0; away from 1 the oracle is an UNBIASED but NOISELESS reading of a noisy strike. This is a KNOWN, DECLARED optimism, not a hidden one.

liveCallers.note: every live caller passes the default (src/ai/PlayerBrain.ts:1321 passes an EXPLICIT 1; the others omit the argument entirely) — the axis is dormant, exactly as the contract's §0 records. Read by a BALANCED-PAREN argument split, not a regex (see the §2 correction note).

whereTheClampsBite.arithmetic: d ≤ (9 − 8.2)/0.6 = 1.3333 m → the base pins at 9 m/s; d ≥ (22 − 8.2)/0.6 = 23 m → the base pins at 22 m/s.
whereTheClampsBite.headline: THE CLAMP BITES ON THE DISTANCE→PACE MAP, NEVER ON THE POWER AXIS. Inside a distance band the base is a CONSTANT and the multiplier scales it exactly; beyond 23 m EVERY ball is the same 22 m/s base, which is precisely the "one pace per range" the contract's §0 names — and precisely where a weight choice has the MOST to add.

expressibleRegion.derivation: ⭐ THE λ_LIN IDIOM (BU-T0b): find the faithful region, CAP AT ITS EDGE, never invent a transform. The multiplier is faithful on the WHOLE line inside the oracle (the launch law is exactly linear in it) — what bounds it is the SIM's own `clamp(powerChoice, 0.85, 1.15)`. Any rung outside that interval is priced by the oracle and NOT struck by the sim ⇒ UNEXPRESSIBLE. The region is therefore the shipped clamp itself, taken verbatim.
expressibleRegion.executionEnvelopeNote: the EXECUTED power can wander to [0.7, 1.3] through the technique error — that is a CONSEQUENCE of a choice, never a choice. The chooser's region is the INTENDED clamp.

whatTheEngineChargesToday: 1. THE FREE ZONE — `attemptFirstTouch` returns CLEAN without rolling when the closing speed ≤ 6 m/s, and ALWAYS for a GK (src/sim/mechanics.ts).

2. THE SPEED TERM — `touchFailChance`: clamp01((s − 6)/8) · 0.07, i.e. the SHIPPED curve SATURATES at 14 m/s and its whole span is worth 0.07 raw pFail units (× 0.875 for a generic receiver ⇒ 0.06125 absolute).
3. THE HARD CEILING — the whole prior is clamped to 0.4.
4. THE ORACLE — `passOptionValue.mirroredTouchFailChance` restates the SAME curve and publishes `touchFailPrior`; a contract test pins the two equal.

5. ⭐⭐ THE CHOOSER-FACING GAP — the published OPTION ladder (L1∧L2∧L3∧L4, the definition BU-C0/BU-T1 and this census use) reads flight, race and corridor. It does NOT read `touchFailPrior` at all. At the ladder's own grain a faster ball is therefore STRICTLY BETTER AT ZERO COST — the dominance hazard, structurally.

6. THE BANKED ALTERNATIVE — `TOUCH_SPEED_COST.heavy` (span 16, weight 0.24) already ships in src, flag-selected per call (`match.edsTouchCost`, OFF in the walked world). Its saturation lands at 22 m/s = the ground-pass launch cap 22 m/s — a DERIVED receiving cost, already in the substrate, not taste.

overshootDefinitions.overrunLaw: rolledDistance(arrivalSpeed, max(0, receiverArrival − ballArrival)) — the engine's OWN closed form (src/sim/carryBeat.ts), fed with the oracle's own two arrival times. OVERSHOOT ⇔ that distance exceeds CONTROL_RADIUS.
overshootDefinitions.restLaw: D∞ = arrivalSpeed / BALL_FRICTION_K — carryBeat's own roll-out endpoint law. The OUT face asks whether targetPoint + dir·D∞ leaves the pitch (|x| > 31.499999999999996 or |y| > 20.299999999999997).
overshootDefinitions.caveat: ⚠ BOTH are ORACLE-GEOMETRY faces on an UNTOUCHED ball: the engine's real receiver usually DOES touch it. They bound the overshoot pressure, they do not predict balls out.

nonClaims: ⭐ INSTRUMENT-ONLY: nothing is armed, nothing is built, no seam acquires a caller, and `src/**` is byte-untouched.
The ladder answers "could the engine's own machinery get the ball there first at this ball speed" — CAPABILITY, never CHOICE (#200). No usage number exists in this stage.
The rung rows are ORACLE re-evaluations of the SAME walked world, not counterfactual sims: nobody actually passed harder. What is measured is the option SET a chooser would see.

The execution error is NOT in these rows: the oracle prices the INTENDED ball. Every rung row away from 1.0 is therefore an OPTIMISTIC reading of what would really be struck; the physics audit states the σ and the chooser slice must carry it.
The overshoot faces are geometry on an UNTOUCHED ball; the sim's receiver usually touches it.
The chooser-slice recommendation in the stage doc is ARITHMETIC over these rows; the ORDER itself is the commander's to bind.
